pl6086187.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl6086187.description: Archaeological site at the interfleuve of the Yenisei and Khemchik Rivers in Tuva. The site, which flooded by the construction of the Sayano-Shushenskaya power plant in the mid-1980s, contained artifacts from the Neolithic through the Medieval periods.

pl809122829.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl809122829.description: Settlement in the Middle Yenisei containing finds dated to the 13th century BCE.

pl95703249.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl95703249.description: Mound site in Khakassia containing burials associated with the Bronze Age Karasuk culture.

pl715491726.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl715491726.description: Cemetery site in Khakassia containing numerous burials associated with the Karasuk Culture (14th-8th centuries BCE). The site was inundated following the construction of the Krasnoyarsk Hydroelectric Power Plant.

pl809343802.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl809343802.description: An early Scythian burial mound located in what is now the Tuva Republic of Russia.

q104232.dateNote: A fort called Achinsk was first built in 1641 and moved to the present site in 1683.

q875.dateNote: Wikidata gives only a century (shown as 1800). Its first written mention is 1675, and it became a town in 1931.

cur-fossil-afontova-gora.dateNote: In 1884 Ivan Savenkov found stone tools and the bones of Ice Age animals on Afontova Gora, a hill in Krasnoyarsk, Siberia. DNA from a bone found here, read in 2014, links its people to the first Americans. About 17,000 years old (0.017 million years).
cur-fossil-afontova-gora.summary: A Siberian hill whose Ice Age people were related to the first Americans.

pl29276714.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl29276714.description: Large (120 meters in diameter) burial mound outside the modern village of Arzhan in the Tuva Republic, with remains dated to the early Scythian period (8th-7th centuries BCE).
